Model MAE
How many points the model misses a final margin by, on average. Lower is better.
Market
The same measure for the closing betting line. It is the benchmark, and has not yet been beaten.
Brier skill
How much better its win probabilities are than always guessing the base rate. Zero would mean it knows nothing beyond how often home teams win.
Calib err
How far its stated confidence sits from what happens. Under 2% means a 70% call really does win about 70% of the time.

Southern Miss gives up 235 rushing yards a game, 137th of 138, which is less a run defense than a polite suggestion. That is why Troy is favored by double digits despite scoring 21 a game, 112th. The model has Troy by 10.7. The market has them by 10.5. Congratulations to everyone involved for agreeing. Southern Miss is 1-3, lost by 28 to UConn and by 35 at Auburn, and converts a third of its third downs into a Troy defense ranked 30th on them. The spread and the over at 50.5 are both coin flips, the over the weaker of two nothings. Troy should win, 74%; the number is already right.

Sharmane says AI read · unmeasured

Arizona State is a 20.5-point favorite while allowing 31.75 points a game, 121st, and turning it over twice a game, 125th. It lost 55-19 at home to Baylor. Hawai'i is no lifeboat, though: 1-4 against a soft schedule, 86 rushing yards a game, 136th, and losses to San José State and Wyoming. Hawai'i +20.5 is the stronger read at 63%, mostly because three touchdowns is a lot of trust in this Arizona State defense. The over at 51.5 is a coin flip and the weaker. Eighty percent for the Sun Devils to win; the margin is the argument.
